scope: Actual root-bound v2 raw geometry versus all frozen 80 source neighbors, retaining KEEP17 and all five previous same-macro precise assets. Source footprints and source roof heights are estimates; this does not replace screening the existing precise meshes.
projection_method: Decode indexed static triangles and active node transforms; map glTF [east,up,-north] to source [east,north,up]. An STRtree queries every actual polygon/line/point projection. Union only the actual clipped intersections per neighbor. A convex hull is diagnostic only.
height_annotation_note: Nearly degenerate projected triangles whose affine height interpolation is unstable use conservative full actual triangle z bounds, explicitly flagged per triangle. Actual height-prism intersection uses independent 3D clipping and does not depend on this annotation.
height_method: Clip every actual intersecting 3D triangle to each source [base,base+height] slab by horizontal-plane edge interpolation, then intersect projected clipped surfaces with original and 10-micrometre-inset neighbor polygons. Count zero-area vertical face intersections too; never waive a wall merely because its planar overlap area is zero.

numeric_policy.acceptance_rule: No actual triangle projection clipped to the estimated source height slab may intersect the polygon after the 10-micrometre boundary inset; even line/point intersections are retained. No height uncertainty allowance is applied. Raw overlaps are always disclosed.

limitations: This is a mapped-source estimated-height prism screen, not a survey of adjacent building roofs or legally surveyed parcel boundaries.
An overhang above an estimated neighbor roof is explicitly reported and requires human interpretation; the height source does not establish real-world separation.
No navigation, camera, source-ground support, runtime collision, rendering, material, interior, or complete model acceptance is performed.
The screen checks actual triangle surfaces and projections; it is not a watertight-solid collision or structural analysis.
